quote: the horizon whose meridian crowns Jerusalem
note: Dante tells the hour by the whole globe. The sun is setting at Jerusalem: it has reached the horizon of the place where the meridian, the arc through the top of the sky, passes over the city. Purgatory stands exactly opposite Jerusalem, so the two share one horizon: the sun going down there is the sun coming up here.
For Dante the river marks the eastern edge of the inhabited world, a quarter of the globe east of Jerusalem. It is midnight there.
The constellation Libra. Dante pictures night as a figure circling the sky opposite the sun. The sun is in Aries, so night is in Libra, on the other side of the zodiac.

quote: when she grows too heavy with darkness
note: After the autumn equinox the nights grow longer than the days. By then the sun has moved into Libra, so the Scales are no longer in the night sky: night has dropped them.
The Roman goddess of dawn. Her cheeks age as the sun comes up: the sky goes from white to rose to gold.
The red planet, glowing redder through the mist low over the sea. Medieval science explained the color by vapors around the planet.
A prayer for his own salvation. To see the angel's light again, Dante must die in grace and be carried here in the same boat.
The angel who ferries the saved to Purgatory. He is the counterpart of Charon, the demon boatman who carries the damned across Acheron in Inferno 3.
Angels serve throughout Purgatory. One guards the gate, and one stands at the stair of each terrace to send the cleansed soul on.
An answer to Ulysses, who crossed this same ocean by human effort alone and said he made wings of his oars (Inferno 26). The angel needs only the wings God gave him.
The boat carries souls, which weigh nothing, so it rides on top of the water. In Inferno 3 Charon told Dante that a lighter boat would carry him one day. This is the one he meant.

quote: When Israel went out of Egypt!
note: The opening of Psalm 114, which Dante gives in Latin: In exitu Israel de Aegypto. It sings of the Exodus, the escape of the Hebrews from slavery. In his Convivio, Dante uses this same verse to show how Scripture carries a spiritual meaning: the soul going out from sin.
At the moment the sun rises in Aries, Capricorn stands at the top of the sky. It has now moved past that point, so the sun is fully up.
Dante's Italian says "pilgrims". Virgil knew the road through Hell, having gone down it once before (Inferno 9). On this mountain he has never been, and he often has to ask the way.

quote: another route so rough and steep
note: The road through Hell.
The olive was the sign of peace. A messenger bringing good news carried a branch of it.
What Purgatory is for. The souls are already saved. The suffering ahead strips away what sin left on them, until they are fit to be seen by God.

context: The failed embrace is modeled on Aeneid 6, where Aeneas tries three times to put his arms around the shade of his father, Anchises, and three times it slips through his hands.
The first soul Dante speaks with in Purgatory is a friend. In Hell the first was Francesca, a stranger. The talk here is easy and affectionate from the start.

quote: to return once more to where I am
note: Dante is making this journey alive so that he may come back to this shore after his death: that is, so that he may be saved.

quote: so much time been taken from you
note: Casella evidently died some time ago, yet he is only now arriving. Dante wants to know what kept him.

quote: The one who takes whoever he pleases
note: The angel boatman, who decides which souls to take and when. Casella doesn't say why he was passed over, only that the angel's will follows God's justice.

Pope Boniface VIII proclaimed 1300 a Jubilee year, with full pardon of sins for pilgrims to Rome. The pardon was counted from Christmas 1299, a little over three months before this Easter. Dante imagines it reaching the dead as well: since then the angel has refused no one.

quote: where the Tiber's waters grow salty
note: The mouth of the Tiber at Ostia, the port of Rome. The souls of the saved gather there to wait for the angel's boat. The way to salvation starts from Rome, the seat of the Church.

context: The dead go to one of two shores: the damned to the bank of Acheron, the saved to the mouth of the Tiber.

note: Dante isn't sure what the dead are allowed to keep. Cato has just said that a new law cut him off from his love for Marcia.

quote: Love that speaks to me within my mind
note: The first line of a poem by Dante himself: "Amor che ne la mente mi ragiona". He later set it at the head of Book 3 of his Convivio and explained the lady it praises as Philosophy. Casella sings Dante's own words back to him.
Even Virgil is caught up in the song. This is the fault he will reproach himself for at the start of Canto 3.

context: He reappears only to scold. The song is no sin, but the souls have work to do, and lingering over an old pleasure is the first weakness the mountain has to cure.

note: The dead skin a snake sheds. The traces of sin cover the soul like an old skin and keep it from seeing God.
Doves were birds of love. Dante compared the lovers Paolo and Francesca to doves in Inferno 5. These doves drop what they were enjoying and fly.

quote: like people going they know not where
note: No one here knows the mountain yet. The souls run toward it without a path, and Dante and Virgil are no better off.
